questions.q: An object's OWD is set to Public Read/Write. What happens when a user tries to use the Sharing button on a record of that object?
options: There's nothing meaningful left to grant, since every user already has full access — the option effectively has nothing to add
It grants Read/Write/Transfer automatically
It throws a permissions error and blocks the user
It automatically converts the grant into a sharing rule
questions.explain: Manual sharing only matters when OWD leaves a visibility gap to fill, which happens under Private or Public Read Only. With Public Read/Write, every user already has full access, so there's nothing left for a manual share to add.

questions.q: What field on a Share object record (like OpportunityShare) identifies why a particular sharing grant exists?
options: AccessLevel
RowCause
OwnerId
ParentId
questions.explain: RowCause records the reason a given Share row exists — 'Manual' for a manual share, a sharing rule's identifier for rule-based shares, or a custom reason for Apex managed shares.

questions.q: A manual share was created by User A on a record while they owned it. The record's ownership is later transferred to User B. What happens to the manual share User A created?
options: It transfers automatically to apply to User B's ownership context
It stays exactly as it was, permanently, regardless of ownership changes
It is automatically removed, since it no longer makes sense once ownership has changed
It converts into a sharing rule automatically
questions.explain: Salesforce automatically removes manual shares when record ownership changes, since the grant was tied to the specific ownership context it was created under and no longer makes sense once that context changes.

questions.q: How does Apex managed sharing (covered in Lesson 8) relate to the mechanism underlying manual sharing?
options: They are completely unrelated mechanisms built on different underlying objects
Apex managed sharing replaces manual sharing entirely and manual sharing no longer functions once Apex sharing is enabled
Apex managed sharing only works for objects where manual sharing has been explicitly disabled
Apex managed sharing uses the exact same `<Object>Share` object pattern, just written to programmatically with its own custom RowCause
questions.explain: Both manual sharing and Apex managed sharing write rows to the same `<Object>Share` object — manual sharing uses RowCause = 'Manual', while Apex managed sharing uses a custom RowCause the developer defines, exposing sharing reasons the declarative UI doesn't offer.

questions.q: An architect reviews an org and finds the same two roles receiving manual shares on similar records, over and over, every week. What should this pattern suggest to the architect?
options: Nothing — this is exactly the intended, sustainable use of manual sharing
That OWD should immediately be set to Public Read/Write to eliminate the need for sharing entirely
That the requirement has outgrown manual sharing and should be redesigned as a sharing rule, team, or Apex managed sharing instead
That manual sharing is broken and should be disabled org-wide
questions.explain: Manual sharing is meant for genuinely one-off, ad hoc grants. A repeating pattern between the same roles signals a structural, repeatable requirement that belongs in a declarative mechanism instead, since manual sharing scales only to one user's one-time judgment call at a time.
